messages:
sam_support: FYI: AcmePay reports 5-8s tail latency and sporadic 401s this morning. They say traffic from EU users is landing in us-east. Escalating.
ivan_netops: ah - any customer request ids or example IPs?
sam_support: yes — customer provided request-id=req_0a9f and client IP 185.73.22.114. Seen spikes starting ~08:10 UTC. TTL on their DNS is 300.
kevin_runtime: digging — initial look shows that IP geolocates to NL but our edgenode routing table maps it to us-east AS path. Possibly GeoIP DB mismatch or anycast deviate.
maya_sre: can you paste the traceroute from the customer? also ask them to run `dig +trace @8.8.8.8 acme.redwood.ai` and `dig @resolver +short txt edns-client-subnet` if possible.
sam_support: pasted below from customer: \n```
traceroute to acme.redwood.ai (34.201.45.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.4 ms
 7  93.184.220.1  48.2 ms
 9  34.201.45.12  180.3 ms
```
kevin_runtime: that ip (34.201.45.12) is in our us-east pool. Looks like resolver is returning us-east anycast for that client subnet. Do we have recent GeoIP db updates?
ivan_netops: MaxMind updated country file yesterday, but our edge mapping import should have run in the morning cron. I see the import job S3 checksum mismatch at 07:50 UTC — could be a partial import that left stale mapping. Filing infra ticket.
maya_sre: possible compounded problem: stale GeoIP -> wrong anycast mapping -> request goes to us-east where auth tokens are validated against eu keys -> 401. Also cross-region TLS termination could be failing with our auth proxy.
sam_support: customer also attached curl showing 401: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://acme.redwood.ai/v1/chat -i` response: 401 x-request-id=req_0a9f.
kevin_runtime: next steps: 1) ivan, revert import or re-run with verified file. 2) maya, confirm auth-key alias routing works across regions (or add temporary alias mapping so eu tokens validate in us-east while we restore). 3) ask customer to flush local resolver cache or test with `+short` against 1.1.1.1.
ivan_netops: re-run import now. watching logs. if job fails again will force a safe rollback to previous db and trigger edge-service restart.
ops-bot: INC-4521 created: "GeoIP import failure -> misroute -> AcmePay 401/latency" assigned to ivan_netops, severity=high.
ivan_netops: import completed at 08:36 UTC and rolled back to prior stable file. Pushed mapping refresh to edge nodes.
kevin_runtime: good. now need to validate propagation. sam, can you ask AcmePay to run `dig @<their-resolver> +short acme.redwood.ai` and `dig +short TXT edns-client-subnet` and paste results? also get a tcpdump around the request-id if they can.
sam_support: asked and waiting. gave suggested command for them to clear DNS: `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` (Linux) or `ipconfig /flushdns` (Windows).
maya_sre: while we wait, temporary mitigation: add a routing override for AcmePay's ASN in our smart-routing table to prefer eu-west for their IP prefixes. kevin, can you apply?
kevin_runtime: applying override now to canary nodes only (to limit blast radius). deploy-bot: canary route override to prefer eu-west for ASN 40045 deployed to 3/20 edge nodes.
kevin_runtime: override live on canary. monitoring latency and 401 rate.
ivan_netops: propagation logs show most edge nodes pulled new mapping by 08:48 UTC. Still seeing 2% of hits to us-east from that IP block — likely external resolver cache. TTL was 300 so caches can hold for up to 5 minutes beyond update.
sam_support: customer confirmed reduced latency for some users but a handful still hit us-east. They ran `dig +trace` and got us-east answers from their ISP's resolver.
maya_sre: that's consistent — ISP resolver cache needs to expire. Ask customer for list of affected ISPs/users — we can add a temporary route pin for their prefixes or escalate to our CDN partner.
kevin_runtime: opening support ticket with CDN partner to request cache purge for the anycast entry. ivan, can you confirm whether our fallback policy still points eu->us for capacity reasons? we don't want automatic fallback causing loops.
ivan_netops: fallback policy currently allows cross-region fallback if edge capacity < 20%. That policy triggered at 08:11 when a transient load spike hit eu-west. I'm going to tighten canary thresholds and disable auto-fallback for AcmePay tenant.
sam_support: AcmePay says 401s dropped to near zero after override, only 3 users reporting issues now. they're happy for now but want root cause analysis and an RCA timeline.
kevin_runtime: ack — we'll prepare RCA: timeline, GeoIP import failure root cause (checksum mismatch), steps taken (rollback, mapping refresh, routing override, CDN purge request), and preventive actions (add checksum alert, better import retries, lower fallback aggressiveness, make tenant pinning easier).
maya_sre: I'll own the postmortem. tagging ops-bot to schedule a blameless RCA doc template.
ops-bot: RCA-186 scheduled. owner=maya_sre. due=2026-03-20.
sam_support: thanks all — keeping thread open until RCA draft. AcmePay says they appreciate the quick response. :thumbsup:
kevin_runtime: thanks team — monitoring for 2h then will close if stable.
